Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. - NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

# api

hazy's backend — a **Hono Worker** (`hazy-api`) for `api.hz.nknighta.me`.
Extracted from `apps/hazy`'s old `/api/v1/**` route handlers. See `README.md`
for the route surface.

# Layout

- `@/*` → `./src/*` (tsconfig paths). The `lib/*` files moved verbatim from
  `apps/hazy/src/lib` keep their imports because of this.
- `src/app.ts` builds the Hono app (CORS, `onError`, routers). `src/index.ts` is
  the Worker entry; `src/server.ts` is local dev on `@hono/node-server`.
- `src/routes/*` — one Hono sub-app per group. Ported route handlers: `c.get("user")`
  for the auth'd user, `c.req.param()/.query()/.json()`, `zod .parse()` (caught by
  `onError`), `return ok(data, { status })`.
- `src/middleware/auth.ts` — `@clerk/backend` verifies the `Authorization: Bearer`
  token, resolves/creates the internal `users` row.
- `src/lib/api/response.ts` — `ok()` / `fail()`, plain `Response.json` (not
  `NextResponse`). Envelope: `{ data }` / `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`.

# Rules

- **Contract types live in `@repo/api-client`** (`packages/api-client/src/types.ts`),
  re-exported here as `@/types/api`. Add a DTO there, add the client method in
  `packages/api-client/src/client.ts`, then the route here — and update the
  matching genre file in `docs/ai/flutter/` (Flutter client reference).
- DB via `getDb()` (`@/db` → `@repo/db`). Schema changes → `packages/db` only.
- Runtime = workerd (prod) / Node (dev). `process.env` is populated from
  `wrangler.jsonc` vars + `wrangler secret`. Keep the `lib/*` code Workers-safe
  (no `fs`, no `node:*` beyond what's already there).
- `bun run dev --filter=api` (Node, :8787, reads `.dev.vars`).
  `bun run deploy --filter=api` = `wrangler deploy`. Secrets: `wrangler secret put`
  from `apps/api/` (never in `wrangler.jsonc`).

# Package manager

`bun`. `bun add <pkg> --filter api`. One `bun.lock` at the repo root.

The only X.com/Twitter-specific handling is a client-side UI hint added in commit `8aac118` that just links out to fxtwitter.com — it does not fetch, download, or process anything itself. --- ### 1. What the fxtwitter hint currently does (exact behavior) File: `apps/hazy/src/components/save/save-url-dialog.tsx` (lines 22–35, 44, 88–99) ```ts /** x.com / twitter.com URLs block scraping, so metadata + images never come * through — fxtwitter.com mirrors the same path and actually serves them. */ function fxtwitterUrl(raw: string): string | null { let parsed: URL; try { parsed = new URL(raw); } catch { return null; } const host = parsed.hostname.replace(/^www\./, ""); if (host !== "x.com" && host !== "twitter.com") return null; parsed.hostname = "fxtwitter.com"; return parsed.toString(); } ``` - It's a pure string transform: if the pasted URL's host is `x.com`/`twitter.com` (with or without `www.`), it swaps the hostname to `fxtwitter.com` and keeps path/query/fragment. - `const fxUrl = useMemo(() => fxtwitterUrl(url.trim()), [url]);` (line 44) recomputes on every keystroke in the save-URL dialog's URL input. - When `fxUrl` is truthy, the dialog renders a plain `` link with a Download icon and the i18n string `t("fxtwitterHint")` (lines 88–99): - en: `"Want the images? Open this post on fxtwitter"` (`apps/hazy/messages/en.json:52`) - ja: `"画像をダウンロードするなら fxtwitter で開く"` (`apps/hazy/messages/ja.json:52`) - Clicking it just opens `fxtwitter.com/...` in a new browser tab. **It does not change what gets submitted/saved** — the user still has to manually paste the fxtwitter URL into the field themselves (or copy it) if they want Hazy's own metadata fetch to hit fxtwitter instead of x.com. Nothing in `apps/api` special-cases fxtwitter or x.com domains during actual metadata fetching. - Same commit (`8aac118`) also added unrelated click-to-edit fields for item `title`/`domain` (new `apps/hazy/src/components/item/editable-field.tsx`, `PATCH /v1/items/:id` gains a `domain` field in `apps/api/src/routes/items.ts:142`, `packages/api-client/src/client.ts` `ItemPatch.domain`, `docs/ai/flutter/items.md`). This is a workaround for the fact that x.com metadata scraping fails — it lets a user manually fix up the title/site name after the fact. Full commit stat: ``` apps/api/src/routes/items.ts | 1 + apps/hazy/messages/en.json | 7 +- apps/hazy/messages/ja.json | 7 +- apps/hazy/src/components/item/editable-field.tsx | 111 +++ apps/hazy/src/components/item/item-detail-view.tsx | 48 ++-- apps/hazy/src/components/save/save-url-dialog.tsx | 32 ++- docs/ai/flutter/items.md | 1 + packages/api-client/src/client.ts | 1 + ``` ### 2. Other x.com/twitter.com references (not fxtwitter) - `apps/hazy-note/lib/db/repo.ts:61` — `kindFromUrl()`: `if (u.includes("twitter.com") || u.includes("x.com") || u.includes("bsky")) return "thread";` — purely classifies the saved item's `SourceKind` as `"thread"` for UI labeling in the separate hazy-note app. No fxtwitter mirroring, no image handling. - `apps/hazy-note/lib/extract.ts:101` looks for `twitter:title` meta tag as a title fallback (standard Twitter Card meta parsing), unrelated to fxtwitter. ### 3. Is there ANY image-downloading/proxying functionality? **No.** Across `apps/api`, `apps/hazy`, `apps/hazy-note`, and `packages/*`, images are handled purely as **external URL strings** — never fetched, downloaded, stored in a bucket, or proxied through the backend: - `packages/db/src/schema.ts:89-90` — `savedUrls` table: `faviconUrl: text("favicon_url")`, `ogImageUrl: text("og_image_url")` — plain text columns holding the original external URL. - `apps/api/src/lib/metadata/fetch-metadata.ts` (the `fetchUrlMetadata` function, full contents read — see below) extracts `og:image` and favicon `` hrefs and resolves them to **absolute URLs** via `absoluteUrl()` (`new URL(href, base).toString()`), but never `fetch()`s the image bytes themselves. - `apps/hazy/src/components/library/item-card.tsx:14` and `apps/hazy/src/components/item/item-detail-view.tsx:96-99` render `` directly (with a biome-lint-disable comment noting it's "arbitrary external OG image, not worth next/image's overhead") — the browser fetches the image straight from the original host, not proxied through Hazy's own infra. - `apps/hazy/src/components/collections/collection-preview.tsx` and `apps/api/src/routes/collections.ts:25-49` build a collection preview thumbnail by collecting up to N `ogImageUrl` strings — again just URLs, no downloading. - `apps/hazy-note/lib/extract.ts` mirrors the same pattern (`ogImage` field is a resolved absolute URL string only). - Searched broadly for `R2`, `bucket`, `S3`, `storage`, `proxy.*image` — no hits related to image storage. The only "R2" mentions are commented-out Next.js/OpenNext **incremental cache** config (`apps/hazy/open-next.config.ts:3,6`, `apps/hazy-note/open-next.config.ts:5`), unrelated to user images. This confirms: since x.com/twitter.com blocks the metadata scraper's `User-Agent`/fetch entirely (per the code comment at `save-url-dialog.tsx:22-23`, "x.com blocks metadata/image scraping"), there's currently no server-side fallback that would fetch images from fxtwitter or anywhere else — the fxtwitter hint is purely a manual, client-side workaround for the human user. ### 4. Prior "X image download" feature that was implemented then removed? **None found.** Checked thoroughly: - All branches: `master`, `dev`, `remotes/origin/master`, `remotes/origin/dev`, plus an `entire/8aac118-e3b0c4` checkpoint branch (an auxiliary branch from the "Entire" checkpoint tool, not a feature branch). - `git log --all --oneline -- '**/*image*'` → **no results**. - `git log --all --grep="image" -i --oneline` → only `8aac118` itself (the fxtwitter hint commit) — no other commit message mentions "image". - `git log --all --grep="download" -i --oneline` → only `5b0ca6e feat: Turborepo monorepo + hazy-note as a working notes app` (an unrelated large initial-import commit, not an image-download feature — the Download icon usage in the fxtwitter hint doesn't correspond to a separate "download" commit either). - Total commit count across all refs: 112 — this is a small/young repo, so this history is essentially complete, not truncated. Conclusion: the fxtwitter hint added in `8aac118` is the **first and only** piece of Twitter/X-specific code that has ever existed in this repo. No prior download/proxy attempt was built and reverted. ### 5. Metadata fetch pipeline — where a follow-up implementation would hook in **Core fetcher:** `apps/api/src/lib/metadata/fetch-metadata.ts` — exports `fetchUrlMetadata(url: string): Promise`. - Fetches the HTML via `fetch()` with an 8s timeout (`FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`), custom UA `"HazyBot/1.0 (+https://hazy.app; link preview fetcher)"`. - Requires `content-type` to include `text/html`/`xhtml`, else returns `{status: "error"}`. - Parses with `cheerio/slim` (Workers-safe, parse-only build — see comment at top of file, lines 1-4). - Extracts: `title` (og:title → ``), `description` (og:description → meta description), `ogImageUrl` (`meta[property="og:image"]` resolved to absolute URL via `absoluteUrl()`), `faviconUrl` (`link[rel=icon|shortcut icon|apple-touch-icon]` → fallback `/favicon.ico`), `contentLanguage` (html lang attr or CJK-density heuristic), `extractedText` (body text, capped at 4000 chars), `estimatedReadMinutes` (word count / 200 wpm). - Returns `FetchMetadataResult = {status:"success", metadata: FetchedMetadata} | {status:"error", error: string}`. **Callers (where a hook would go):** `apps/api/src/routes/items.ts` - `POST /v1/items` (create, lines ~87-131): calls `fetchUrlMetadata(cleanUrl)` after `parseAndNormalizeUrl(url)` (from `apps/api/src/lib/metadata/normalize-url.ts`), then inserts a `savedUrls` row with `title`/`description`/`faviconUrl`/`ogImageUrl`/`extractedText`/`contentLanguage`/`estimatedReadMinutes`/`fetchStatus`. - `POST /v1/items/:id/refetch` (lines ~177-206): same `fetchUrlMetadata` call against the existing stored `url`, updates the same columns. - Both are the natural integration points if you wanted to special-case x.com/twitter.com URLs server-side (e.g., rewrite to fxtwitter.com before calling `fetchUrlMetadata`, or add a separate image-download step after metadata fetch succeeds). **Serialization:** `apps/api/src/lib/serializers.ts:16` — `serializeSavedUrl()` passes `ogImageUrl` straight through from the DB row to the API DTO. **DB schema:** `packages/db/src/schema.ts:77-90` (`savedUrls` table) — `faviconUrl`/`ogImageUrl` are `text` columns (external URLs only, no blob/asset table exists). **API contract types:** `packages/api-client/src/types.ts:18` (`ogImageUrl: string | null` on the item DTO) and `packages/api-client/src/client.ts` `ItemPatch`. **Frontend consumers:** `apps/hazy/src/components/library/item-card.tsx:12-14`, `apps/hazy/src/components/item/item-detail-view.tsx:96-99`, `apps/hazy/src/components/collections/collection-preview.tsx`, `apps/hazy/src/components/collections/collection-detail-view.tsx:39` — all just `<img src={ogImageUrl}>` or pass the URL through. **Separate parallel pipeline (hazy-note app, not yet migrated to `apps/api`):** `apps/hazy-note/lib/extract.ts` — `fetchAndExtract(url)`, a dependency-free regex-based HTML extractor (no cheerio) with its own `ogImage`/`favicon` extraction (lines 110-119), called from `apps/hazy-note/lib/db/repo.ts` (e.g. line 287: `ogImageUrl: extracted.ogImage ?? existing.ogImageUrl`). Per `apps/hazy-note/CLAUDE.md`, this app "still has its own `/app/api/*` route handlers" and hasn't been moved behind `apps/api` yet — so a follow-up feature touching X/Twitter image handling would need to be applied in **both** places if hazy-note should get it too, unless only `apps/hazy` + `apps/api` are in scope. ### Recommendation for a follow-up implementation Since there's no existing download/proxy infra to reuse, a real "download X images" feature would need net-new work: likely (a) detecting x.com/twitter.com URLs server-side and rewriting to fxtwitter.com before/instead of the direct fetch in `fetchUrlMetadata`/`fetchAndExtract` (fxtwitter's API also exposes more media than a single og:image, e.g. `/status/ID.json` or embed endpoints, worth checking if multiple images per tweet matter), and (b) if actual image bytes should be persisted (not just URL passthrough), a new storage layer (R2 bucket, etc.) would need to be introduced from scratch — nothing like that exists in `packages/db` or `wrangler.jsonc` today.
